## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Zhānbó bǐqiū jīng* is a single-fascicle Western Jìn 西晉 translation of a discourse delivered by the Buddha at Campā 瞻婆 (恒伽 = the Ganges), beside the Lotus Pool of the Dharma (法賴池), to the assembled monks. The Chinese parallel is T26[122] (the *Zhānbó jīng* 瞻波經 of the *Madhyama-āgama*). The text continues the cycle of *uposatha*-themed discourses set at Campā, of which [T33](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0033), [T34](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0034) and [T35](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0035) are the principal short Chinese versions; T64 differs from these in its specific doctrinal content (the *Madhyama* sūtra 122 in question concerns the eight reasons for which the assembly of monks may be censured — distinct from the eight ocean-similes of T26[37]).

**Abstract**

T64 was produced during Fǎjù's Western Jìn translation period (290–311 CE), recorded in the frontmatter. The Indic source is presumed lost.
